correctness.rationale: For q(z)=Σ_{j=-m}^m a_j z^j with negative highest a_m and strict negative symbol off zero, F_t(z)=exp(tq(z)) has Laurent coefficients p_j(t), is entire on C\{0}, tends to zero along real z→+∞ yet has an essential singularity at infinity. Infinitely many nonzero positive-index coefficients and an eventually one-sign tail would force F_t(r)→±∞ by comparing polynomial positive/negative contributions, so both signs appear infinitely often for each fixed t>0. The n-cycle kernel is the periodization of p_j and eventually tends to rank-one uniform via its spectral gap. Exponential weighted Laurent bounds control aliasing for t<=c n, while the diagonal spectral mass is at least C/sqrt(t); the small-/intermediate-time sign persists by uniform Taylor bounds and compactness, proving linear delay. For Q=D-D²/12, q(16)=-2475/1024 and elementary majorants permit c=1/500; spectral decay implies strict positivity by n²/16 for n>=5. Independent exact stencil checks and numerical cycles n=5..30 corroborate sign behavior. The infinite/time-uniform result rests on analytic inequalities, not finite simulation.
residual_risks: Bounded independent computation is corroborative only; the all-parameter proof is analytical.
